concerns.text: Constitution Principle VI mandates computing the covariance matrix 'for every sample'. Tasks T022a and T022b explicitly reject this, stating a single 4-dim vector cannot form a covariance matrix and instead computing a 'global' eigenvalue. This is a semantic weakening of the constitutional requirement, not a valid mathematical correction. The task must be revised to either implement the per-sample calculation as required or the Constitution must be amended to reflect the mathematical reality before tasks are generated.

Task T037 hardcodes the dataset source as 'UCI/imagenet-rewards' and fails loudly if not found. The Spec (FR-001) and Assumptions refer to the 'Z-Reward evaluation dataset'. If Z-Reward is not hosted at the UCI URL, this task violates the spec's requirement to ingest the specified dataset, creating a brittle dependency not authorized by the spec. The task must support the actual Z-Reward source or the spec must be updated to specify UCI ImageNet Rewards as the canonical source.

FR-003 and SC-004 require the 'primary quality dimension' to be determined 'solely by prompt metadata'. Task T014 defaults to 'Alignment' if the column is missing, and T024 relies on this. The spec does not guarantee a 'primary_dimension' column exists. This task silently relaxes the constraint by allowing a hardcoded fallback, risking circular validation or incorrect dimension selection if the metadata is absent. A task must explicitly verify the metadata field exists or raise an error, rather than silently defaulting.

SC-002 requires the model to demonstrate value via 'statistically significant improvement (p < 0.05 via paired t-test) OR R² > 0.0'. Task T030c implements the t-test but does not explicitly include a check or output for the R² > 0.0 condition as a pass/fail gate. This risks a task completing successfully even if the model has no predictive power (R² <= 0), violating the success criterion's requirement to demonstrate value.
